gizmoOdds.marsCrew30yr: 30% (my estimate, not a program target). No crew-rated Mars transit or landing hardware exists yet, and radiation, Mars entry-descent-landing, and life support at crewed scale are still unsolved problems. But 30 years is a long runway, and SpaceX's iterative hardware pace has repeatedly turned 'aspirational' dates into eventually-delivered hardware — so a crewed landing by 2056 is plausible but far from certain.
gizmoOdds.moonBase30yr: 65% (my estimate, not a program target). Three separate programs — NASA's Artemis Base Camp, China's ILRS, and Blue Origin's commercial plans — are all driving toward sustained Moon surface presence in the 2030s, and the core hardware (Starship, New Glenn, Long March 10, Gateway) is real and flying or in late development. Thirty years absorbs multiple rounds of schedule slips, and a competitive dynamic makes a permanent base more likely, not less.

players.marsDetail: Musk on X (Mar 2025): uncrewed Starship to Mars at end of 2026, human landings 'as soon as 2029, although 2031 is more likely'; the 2026 window was missed, with the uncrewed attempt now aimed at the 2028/29 window (2029 'most likely'). All Musk's Mars dates are aspirational, not program commitments.
players.marsTarget: 2031 — Musk's 'most likely' aspiration for first human landings
players.moonDetail: Starship HLS is NASA's contracted first Artemis lander; NASA's Jared Isaacman said in April 2026 it will fly whichever lander (SpaceX or Blue Origin) is ready first. SpaceX has no separate independent crewed-Moon date beyond Artemis.
players.moonTarget: Artemis IV — early 2028 (as NASA's Starship Human Landing System)

players.marsDetail: Administrator Bill Nelson stated 'humans to walk on Mars by 2040' in the State of NASA address (Mar 2022); NASA's Moon-to-Mars architecture is not a mission or manifest, and as of Aug 2026 NASA publishes no official crewed Mars landing date.
players.marsTarget: 2040 — stated goal, but currently no official crewed Mars landing date
players.moonDetail: NASA's Feb 27, 2026 restructure made Artemis III (NET June 2027) a crewed Earth-orbit docking test instead of a landing; Artemis IV (south pole) is now the first landing, Artemis V follows. Artemis II completed a crewed lunar flyby in April 2026. Long-term goal: a south-pole base/Artemis Base Camp.
players.moonTarget: Artemis IV — early 2028 (first crewed Artemis lunar landing)

players.marsDetail: Blue Origin's Mars work is uncrewed only: NASA's $700M Mars Telecommunications Orbiter (ready by end of 2028, operational ~2030) and New Glenn's launch of NASA's ESCAPADE Mars probes. No crewed Mars target has been announced.
players.moonDetail: NASA contracted Blue Origin for the Artemis V crewed lander ($3.4B, May 2023); an uncrewed Blue Moon demo is targeted for 2027, and a robotic Blue Moon Mark 1 Endurance mission is planned NET fall 2026. Bezos said in an Oct 7, 2026 interview he believes the U.S. can land on the Moon in 2028 — his personal assessment, not a confirmed date.
players.moonTarget: Artemis V — ~2029/2030 (Blue Moon Mark 2 crewed lander, NASA contract)

players.marsDetail: ESA's official Vision (vision.esa.int): 'The ultimate goal is to send Europeans to Mars in the 2050s.' This is a vision statement, not a funded mission date.
players.moonDetail: ESA has no independent crewed Moon landing program or date; it contributes Orion's service module, the Gateway I-HAB module, and astronauts (ESA's Luca Parmitano is on the Artemis III crew). Its Explore 2040 roadmap aspires to have Europeans on the lunar surface 'throughout the 2030s'. Argonaut is a robotic cargo lander (Mission 1 proposed by end of 2030, pending 2025 Ministerial funding).

players.marsDetail: Wang Xiaojun, head of state-owned CALT, presented a three-step roadmap at GLEX 2021 with first crewed Mars launches in 2033 and follow-ups in 2035/2037/2041; a 2025 China Aerospace Studies Institute paper notes Chinese research considers an orbit-only crewed Mars mission by 2050. The 2033 date is a concept/aspiration, not an official CMSA commitment. China's firm Mars target is robotic: Tianwen-3 sample return launches ~2028.
players.marsTarget: 2033 — stated concept (not an official program target)
players.moonDetail: CMSA's stated 'fixed goal': land Chinese astronauts on the Moon by 2030, as a precursor to the International Lunar Research Station (ILRS) moon base in the 2030s. Hardware in development: Long March 10, Mengzhou crew spacecraft, Lanyue lander, moon suits, rover.
